question.text:
Consider a system with:

  • Two-level page tables
  • $42$-bit virtual addresses
  • $40$-bit physical addresses
  •  $8$-byte page-table entries
  •  $64$ KB pages
  •  $64$ KB page tables at each level

Which of the following addresses use the same first-level page-table entry as:

$$\texttt{0x00 123 456 789}$$

  1. $\texttt{0x00 123 444 444}$
     
  2. $\texttt{0x00 0A9 876 789}$
     
  3. $\texttt{0x00 136 345 678}$
     
  4. $\texttt{0x00 000 006 789}$
question.subject: Operating System

question.text:
A byte-addressable machine implements virtual memory with a $4$ MB virtual address space using a three-level page-table system.

All page tables live in physical address space.

The breakdown of virtual-address bits is:

$$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|} 
\hline
\text{L1} & \text{L2} & \text{L3} & \text{Offset} \\
\hline
5 & 5 & 5 & 7 \\
\hline
\end{array}$$

How many PTEs can fit in a frame?
question.subject: Operating System

question.text:
The following table shows some parameters of a virtual memory system:

$$\begin{array}{|c|c|} \hline
\text{Parameter} & \text{Value} \\
\hline
\text{Virtual Address} & 42\ \text{bits} \\
\text{Physical Address} & 40\ \text{bits} \\
\text{Physical Page Size} & 64\ \text{KB} \\
\text{Page Table Entry} & 8\ \text{bytes} \\
\hline
\end{array}$$ In general, the virtual address space of a process is mostly empty. To reduce the size of the page table, a multilevel page table is used for address translation.

How many levels of page tables will be needed for address translation, given that the size of a page table at any level is the size of a physical page?
question.subject: Operating System

question.text:
Consider a virtual memory system that uses 2-level paging.

The page size is: $256=2^8$ bytes

Each individual page table fits exactly into one memory frame, and the size of each page-table entry is: $8$ bytes

What is the maximum size, in bytes, of a virtual address space in this system?
question.subject: Operating System

question.text:
Let us assume there is a two-level page table in your system.

The virtual address is split as:

$\texttt{<vpn part1, vpn part2, page offset>}$

Which of the following statements is true?

  1. $\texttt{vpn part 1}$ is used to index the physical page that contains data.
     
  2. $\texttt{vpn part 1}$ is used to get the base address of the first-level table.
     
  3. Page offset is used to index the TLB.
     
  4. $\texttt{vpn part 2}$ is used to index the PTE in the second-level page table.
question.subject: Operating System
